Appearance: Hiiro has long crimson hair tied in a ponytail, amber brown eyes, and a set of dual colored horns one of which is broken.
He wears a long white shirt, brown pants held up with a belt adorned with large Magatama beads, as well as long white socks and sandals. He also carries aNagamakithat is as long as his body.
Personality: As a strong, passionate and commanding individual, he is shown to value strength and honor first and foremost. He is tormented by survivor's guilt, and seeing the other kijin was enough to quell his murderous rage towardsGeld Junior.

He also shown to be diplomatically aware of his actions and is very polite towards theleaderofTempest. His core trait is his simple solving solutions and not turning away despite the risks or in some cases the chance of being manipulated easily. He cares a greet deal to QueenTowa, because she saved him from death twice.

Hiiro has a bad habit of losing his reasoning to his anger. Simply seeing Geld Junior's group set him off, completely disregarding the fact they were working on the road to Tempest. Even later, despite the fact he was told that he was being used, Hiiro lost himself completely to a violet demon's magic.
Background: Hiiro was anOgreborn in the same village as Benimaru and co. He showed remarkable strength and talent for fighting even from a young age and became close friends with theYoung MasterandPrincess. As he grew he quickly became the strongest in the village, surpassing even their leader and theOld Man, and becoming affectionately called "Brother" by the entire village. Using his mastery with weapons, magic, and mystic-arts as well as his strategic mind he often found himself sparring with and training the rest of the village, teaching them to branch out from the basic fighting stye taught to them by the Old Man and developing new styles that played to their strengths and talents. He noticed Benimaru's affinity for fire and taught himOgre Flame; took note ofShion's immense strength and advised her to use heavy weapons like clubs; and advisedSoueito adopt a second sword into his fighting style among others.

To help support his village he one day decided to venture out as a mercenary alongside a small group of fellow ogres. Eventually, they were hired byClaymanas apart of his army for a period of time. When they heard news of an Orc Army fromOrbicinvading the Jura Forest, they deserted from Clayman’s army against the terms of his contract. As deserters they were tracked down by Clayman’s forces and systematically slaughtered. Hiiro held his own but eventually fell toYamzaafter being caught off guard by hisDoppelgänger. He and his men were retrieved by the nearby kingdom of Raja, with what little medical aid they had being unable to heal their mortal wounds. With little time to make a choice, Raja's Queen, Towa decided to grant Hiiro hisName, hoping it would allow him to survive his injuries. Upon waking up, Hiiro immediately set off to his village on the back of one of Raja's dragons. He arrived at the ruined village, too late to help them fend off the orcs. He decided to return to Raja afterwards, dedicating himself to repaying the debt he owed to the nation’s queen.
Trivia: Despite being referred to as "Brother" by nearly everyone in the Ogre Village, Hiiro has no biological siblings.
He shares a personality trait from each of the surviving Ogres.
He shares the same colors of horns that all known Kijin have; but his left horn was actually broken, and reformed upon being named, became whitened more.
Has shown an anger fuelled state that makes his eyes fiery red, but not the same red that the Anime uses to show merciless fury.

Daemon.title: Daemon

Background: Daemons are derived from theGreat Holy SpiritofDarkness, with theprimordialdaemons being the shadows of theSeven Angels of Originwho were created from the Great Holy Spirit ofLight.

Daemons spontaneously come into being within theDaemon Realmaslesser daemons, where they endlessly fight each other. At times they might be summoned into theCentral World, where they require amaterial bodyto remain permanently or they will get ejected back into the Daemon Realm by the rejection force of the world.

Daemons have an innately strongresistancetomagic, and while without abody, they can use a temporary medium made out ofmagiculesknown as a "magic body" to interact with the material plane. This magic body makes physical attacks borderline useless against them, as even if damaged, they can simply revert it back to its original shape. Once a daemon is incarnated into a physical vessel, their energy sublimates inside of it and begins transforming into something truly their own. Their body, however, does not retain the same benefits as a purely magical corpus as physical attacks are able to harm them. In particular, purely natural effects — such as those produced by elementals — are especially effective against them, as their resistance towards magic is rendered meaningless.
Appearance: Daemons, as spiritual life-forms, possess appearances that are determined entirely by their self-image. Despite this, it is somewhat easy to estimate a daemon's evolutionary stage and age purely on their appearance. Typically, the morehumanthe daemon in question appears, the stronger its ego is, with fully human daemons, excluding those possessing a human body, being eithergreater daemonsof immense age or fearsomearchdaemons. Lesser daemons and younger greater daemons, on the other hand, possess more animalistic and distorted appearances, resembling something more like a hybrid between a human and a horrificmonster. Despite the extreme variety in their appearance, all daemons possess claws, horns, and wings although older daemons can hide them at their discretion.

Most daemons above the lesser daemon stage belong to a specific color lineage, with their color being apparent in their appearance. The color of a daemon's sclera will usually match their lineage and, although not always, other parts of their body match this color as well. Examples include, but are not limited to, hair color, iris color, and skin color. The color of their clothing usually also reflects the color of their lineage.
Summoning: With the use ofSummoning magic, it is possible to summon daemons to the material plane. Daemons summoned this way, assuming their master and task are fair, are fiercely loyal and honor their contracts absolutely. During the duration of their summoning, assuming they aren't provided a material body, their magical corpus is sustained directly by the summoners magic power. It is also possible for daemons to breakdown the corpses of material beings to reinforce their magical corpus for a period of time. One adult human corpse is enough to sustain a greater daemon for three days or an arch daemon for a day and a half.

The act of summoning daemons, while not entirely forbidden, is restricted information. Only high ranking adventurers such asThegisor special individuals such as nobles who have access to royal libraries have the opportunity to learn this brand of summoning magic. Summoning lesser and greater daemons in the first place requires a summoner with a large amount of magical power. Even summoning a lesser daemon is enough to completely tire an A-minusrankadventurer such as in the case of Thegis.

The summoning of archdaemons is a completely heretical and forbidden act. The knowledge is only kept and passed down verbally by select masterwizardsand royal families, and the act itself is so foolish and dangerous that one would have to be utterly insane to even attempt it. Archdaemons possess extremely strong wills and forms that teeter closer to humans in appearance. They're unpredictable and have enough power to easily break the contract that binds them to their summoner. Unless the summoner appeals to the daemons whims or is otherwise strong enough to force them into submission, they are likely to be slaughtered on the spot.
Social class and strength: Daemons grow more powerful the longer they live. However, there is a limit how muchenergya disembodied daemon can amass. This limit is reached when they become archdaemons, making them numerically equivalent in terms of raw power. At this stage knowledge and experience is what matters most. If they are able to break through this limit, they are easily able to reach higher levels of power.

Daemons have social classes mostly based on strength. The stronger a daemon is and the longer they can go without being defeated, the higher their social standing is.[1]Since older daemons are usually more powerful, it is possible to estimate their standing based on their age.
Evolutionary stages: Daemons have their own evolutionary stages, which, unlike their social class, is much more prone to external factors within the material world such as the quality of the contractual compensation, the magicule supply of the summoner, the presence or lack of aname, and other similar elements.
Naming leads to an immediate strength and/orskillgain and in case of a particularly strong namer, an evolution to the next stage might occur.
Color lineage: Daemons are assigned to acolor lineageafter becoming greater daemons. Their color matches one of the primordials' based on their personality. All daemons of a certain color share the basic personality traits of their progenitor, however, they might express these traits in different ways.
Depending on what color lineage a daemon belongs to, their willingness to cooperate is different. There are three major dispositions that are based on their primordials:
Negotiable: Can be negotiated with and are probably the best bet when it comes to contracting with a daemon while keeping the risks at a minimum.

Non-negotiable: It is unlikely for any contract to be formed. At worst, the summoner might even be tricked into a wicked contract that they end up regretting, which is why it's strongly discouraged to summon any daemons from this type of lineage. The only practical use for them would be to trick someone into summoning a daemon of this kind within an enemy nation.

Whimsical: The result of summoning daemons of these lineages can vary and the chances of success for establishing a contract are random. These daemons can be reckless and are subject to mood swings. Their eccentric nature makes them more likely to possess proficiency in areas that other lineages do not possess. There is a risk associated with summoning them, but it is still safer than summoning non-negotiable ones.
Abilities: Daemons possess a natural affinity formagic, especiallyaspectualanddark magic.
Trivia: Daemons are honor-bound to their contracts, so it's up to them if they wish to take the prize they were offered.Testarossa refused to claim the soul of herfriend.Ultima revivedTowaas an apology forLacuaviolating the contract she established.

Human Form: Velgrynd has long, straight, azure blue hair kept in twin buns with black ribbons, while the rest is down her back, and deep gold eyes. Her usual attire consists of a dark-coloredcheongsamwith a goldendragonpattern, as well as white long gloves and white thigh-length boots, both adorned with gold ornaments. She is described as having a very Germanic style of beauty.

When she acts as the Marshal, she changes her form to hide her true identity. In this form, she has short, dark hair styled in a bun, gray eyes, and proper military clothing of theImperial Guardian, mostly black with gold accents. This form is probably her default disguise, with different outfits if needed.
Dragon Form: Her dragon form is similar in size toVeldora's dragon form; however, herbodytakes on a more agile, snake-like shape suitable for flying in the sky. She is covered in crimson red scales with white spikes covering her back. On each side of her body runs a thin line in the same deep golden color as her eyes.
Personality: Fitting her title and attributes, Velgrynd is a hotheaded individual who dislikes complex schemes and often acts on her emotions, but is still highly intelligent. She exudes great confidence in her power, which is why she was utterly stunned whenRimuru, a mere upstartDemon Lord, defeated her. However, unlike her brother Veldora, she readily admits and acknowledges her defeat. Velgrynd has a whimsical nature and is only inclined to help and cooperate with others if they have earned her respect.

When it comes to her friends and family, Velgrynd is very compassionate. In contrast to her sisterVelzard, she is known for her gentleness and her tendency to spoil Veldora the most when disciplining him. Upon thinking that Veldora had been killed by Rimuru's hands, she immediately flew into a rage. However, her anger turned to joy upon discovering that he was alive and well.

The most defining trait of Velgrynd is her unwavering devotion to Rudra. She is willing to go to any lengths and do anything he desires, and anyone who dares to insult Rudra in any way instantly triggers her rage. Velgrynd's interests are primarily aligned with Rudra's, and she pays little attention to other matters unless they hold value in his eyes.
Background: Velgrynd is the embodiment of the concept of acceleration and possesses control overfire. She is the third among the True Dragons to be born, and at some point, she was bestowed with theUltimate skillRaguelby her elder brother,Veldanava, possibly because of the intrinsic nature of acceleration. It is presumed that sometime after this, she met theChosen heroRudra, with whom she eventually fell in love. Together with his sisterLucia, they embarked on a mission to the North to defeatGuy Crimson. However, Rudra recklessly named theDaemon, causing his Divine Spiritual Power to deplete, and he wandered between life and death. She was also present when Rudra and Guy dueled, and during that time, she would argue with her elder sister, Velzard, about how to discipline their newly born brother, Veldora. Some time later, when Rudra and Guy engaged in their game to rule theworld, Rudra established his base in the East, and Velgrynd was one of the individuals who supported him. With her tremendous strength as a True Dragon, they transformed the once small minor Kingdom of Nasca into the GreatEastern Empireby absorbing all the surrounding kingdoms in the East, eventually making Rudra the Emperor.

With the Empire in place as a base, Rudra and Velgrynd established theImperial Guardians, an elite group ofenlightenedhumanswith the potential to become powerful warriors known asSaints. They would occasionally send these warriors off to battle in order for them to gain experience and awaken as Saints, with Velgrynd as the Marshal. Her true identity was kept a secret, and she served as Rudra's greatest pawn and partner against Guy. In an effort to turn the tide of victory against Guy Crimson and help Rudra lessen the burden of controlling the Ultimate SkillMichael, Velgrynd hoped that Veldora would assist her in her endeavor. However, he refused and instead challenged her, but she defeated him, and he fled with his tail between his legs. The aftermath of their battle created a volcanic region near the future city ofEl Dorado.

Unknown to Velgrynd, Rudra was nearing his limit, and he secretly asked bothDamradaandTatsuya Kondouto kill him if he ever lost control. Fortunately, that time never came; however, the Ultimate skill Michael eventually managed to secretly take control of Rudra, turning him into a cruel and mindless puppet.Italso took control of all of Rudra's vassals, including Velgrynd herself, without her knowledge.

It wasn't until she was defeated by aslimenamed Rimuru Tempest that she was finally able to break free from Michael's control. Thanks toCieland Rimuru, she gained a newpowerthat allowed her to search for her beloved Rudra'ssoulacrossspace,time, and even otherworldsuntil only one shard remained. The soul shards she had collected returned to her beloved Rudra, who was now known asMasayuki Honjou. The return of his soul fragments sent the boy back to theCentral World. Velgrynd, now on a new quest to find the boy and reunite with him, used her power and returned to her homeworld.

Summary: SPOILER WARNINGThis article contains information from past the official English translation of the novels. Read at your own risk.
Appearance: Zelanus, just like the rest of the Insectars, had a thickexoskeletonthat surrounded his entirebodylike a suit of armor. His silver colored exoskeleton was made entirely out ofHihi'irokane, down to the tiniest hair. His forehead had two antennae and long blade-covered hairs that went down to the two sets of red wings that adorn his back. On his torso were three sets of arms; with the top pair deforming into bladed weapons, the center pair acting as fists for melee combat, and the bottom pair being specialized for castingmagic. He was capable of sprouting mouths on any part of his body to consume his prey, even the soles of his feet.

In the light novel's illustrations, Zelanus is depicted with an appearance wildly different from his description in the text. He more closely resembles Zegion and lacks most of his features. His exoskeleton is black instead of white, he has only 2 arms instead of 6, he lacks antennae and instead has horns, he has 2 black wings instead of 4 red ones, and he lacks the long silver hair that runs down to his waist. He also has the additions of gold-colored ornaments covering various parts of his exoskeleton and a long centipede-like tail.
Personality: Zelanus, despite having absolute confidence in his strength, could be called a coward who took the utmost precautions against even the slightest possibility of a threat to his safety. He wouldn't show his face on a battlefield until he analyzed all of the enemies capabilities and ensured his safety. Once he determined that there were no threats to himself, he crushed his enemies with his full force, not holding back even against someone he deemed insignificant.

Despite holding the needs and stability of his people in high regard, he was willing to sacrifice as many of them as it took to win, even his own children. He also wasn't the type to work with others, only allowing himself to be ordered byVeldanavaand shirking even the possibility of cooperating with others without an extremely good reason.
Background: Zelanus was the first intelligentcryptidborn from the ruler of the cryptid raceIvaragé'smagicules. His presence was noticed by Veldanava, who proceeded to take Zelanus under his wing and give him a name, much to the annoyance of Feldway. From there, he began to subjugate his cryptid siblings who ran wild unchecked within the underworld. At some point after this, he gave birth toPeliod, whose powers as a "Queen" allowed her to create an untold amount ofInsectoidsthat extended his range of influence in the underworld tremendously. From theInsects, powerfulInsectarswere eventually born and given jobs as the ruling class that managed the numerous insects under them, acting as Zelanus' hands and feet.

The Insectars were named theTwelve Insect GeneralsandZess, the son of Zelanus, was appointed as their commander. From here he maintained a rocky relationship with thePhantomsand their ruler Feldway, with the two only setting aside their differences when the Cryptid population grew out of control and stampeded. When Veldanava perished, Zelanus was quick to dismiss the offer of an alliance from Feldway, later reconsidering when he met withMichaelwho bore a similar presence to Veldanava. To attest to their alliance, Zelanus sentRazulandMinazato theEastern Empireto serve Michael and act as an avant-garde. To act as replacements, and to bolster as much power as possible for the oncoming war, Zelanus had Peliod give birth to a newQueenand he also gave birth to asecond son. However, Zess, taking too much after his father, grew wary of their potential and eventually attacked them, forcing the pair to flee to the Central World.

Appearance: Ivaragé originally had an indeterminate and monstrous form that grew larger and more sinister as its energy continued to grow. After evolving and gaining sentience it was free to choose its own appearance as aspiritual life-form, taking a humanoid form. In its humanoid form, Ivaragé resembles a small child sporting pale skin, soft white hair, and shining golden eyes. It wears a simple dress-like outfit in addition to an oversized scarf adorned with a distinctive brooch or necklace.[1]
After devouring the remains ofLucia Nasca, she would have an identical appearance to the original with exception of small fangs.
After devouring Veldanava, she has a female armored like humanoid appearance that is described to be a mix of Veldanava and Lucia Nasca.
Personality: Ivaragé was originally a being lacking any emotions or coherent thoughts, only moving based on its instinct which compelled it to fight strong opponents and cause mass amounts of destruction. After the events ofA Disturbance in the Royal Capital, it consumed the fallensoulsofObera's army, inheriting their hatred and evolving to gain intelligence, emotions, and desires.[2]

She's a free-spirited and person who does what she wants without a lack of hesitation, being equal parts wicked and charming with the innocence of a child. She has a deep sense of adoration for her family, wanting to reunite with her other-self more than anything and doting on her children with glee. She's beyond envious of living beings and wants nothing more than to rid herself of the loneliness that's arisen in her heart from being separated from her other-half.[1]

She would become more desperate and obsessive to reunite with her other-self as time went on: slowly discarding her care for her children upon her humiliating defeat byGuy Crimson, and, when Veldanava gave her Lucia's memories, even believing she became Lucia Nasca herself, all the while still wishing to become one again throughout it all. Upon renaming herself to Luvelgé all she wanted was to destroy the Multiverse and killRimuru's loved ones just to spite him for his constant interferences.[3]
Background: Before anything and everything, "it" was drifting in the World of Death, a world with no beginning nor end. Fearing change, it slumbered as if dreaming.[4]Then a Will was born, a will without any form or body. It was Omnipotent and Omniscient, as much as a dreamer inside their own dream. As the Will had not taken any form, it was essentially the world itself, Perfection, Completeness, lacking absolutely nothing.[5][6]

However, a part of that will soon grew bored of the unchanging world, a world where it could perceive everything. And so diversity was born, created by two conflicting Wills. One sought freedom and to perceive change, another ought to bear the loneliness, too afraid of the changing world. Thus these wills separated, manifesting as Ivaragé and Veldanava, Destroyer and Creator, Yin & Yang.[4]Their dreamlike sense of Omnipotence was gone, replaced by the forever changing "World".[6]

Unlike Veldanava, who had sought an unpredictable world, Ivarage desired the complete opposite, wanting to reunite with her other-half and "return" to the formless "Will" they both once were. It eventually found its way to the central world and went on a rampage, doing battle with theSeven Angels of OriginandGuy Crimsonbefore ultimately being sealed away in theOtherworldby Veldanava.[7][8]

After being sealed inside the spooky palace for billions of years, it found an opportunity to break free and on a whim consumed the souls ofObera's subordinates. As a result of this Ivaragé inherited their hatred and gained the embers of intelligence, triggering theHalloween Carnivaland evolving into a fully sentient being. Now wide awake and self-aware, she began to remember her origins and missed the comfort of being a complete being. Filled with loneliness, she set out on a mission to consume all worlds as a means to reunite with her other-half and become whole again.[1]

Appearance: Jax is a relatively tall and muscular man with long course hair braided in a style similar to dreadlocks capped with tassels. He wears a dark colored sleeveless shirt and dark pants in addition to a white cloak or half-cape and an animal pelt around his waist. His face is fearsome, with a sharp square jaw and a chiseled aquiline nose offset by a black mark or tattoo along his left eye.
Personality: Jax has a rather rough and crass personality, believing himself to be above everyone else and valuing everyone and everything else very little. He isn't afraid to get his hands dirty and involve himself with criminals or murder those who get in his way. Although his ego is second to none, he does still value the importance of family, becoming enraged at the death of his brotherZachariahand tracking down his killers for revenge.
Background: Jax, as well as his brother Zachariah, were among the various ragtag fighters recruited to join the Rook Geniuses, a famed group of knights that serve only the Holy EmperorLouisand enjoy a high level of status. Jax especially gained infamy and respect within the group for his strength, likely a result of hisUnique skillEminence.

The Six Demon Generals are the Daemon leader servingGuy Crimsonand are the main leader of his army of Daemons in theFrost Palacein theIce Continent. As noted by Guy, while considering their progenitors to be excellent maids, he sees Rain as an idiot and Misery as useless, with the former doing idiotic things behind his back and the latter being unhelpful and unreliable when the time calls for it. Due to this, he mainly relies on the six Daemon Generals to do important work and tasks for him. So much so that he considers some members, such as Misoria, indespensible to him and far more important than her progenitor Rain.

Appearance: A dragonewt's appearance can vary depending on their lineage or, in the case of ones that evolved from lizardmen, their will during their evolution.[1]

Some dragonewts normally don't look much different than lizardmen such in the case ofGabiruand his subordinates. Their scale color may change to be darker, but some don't seem to change their color at all. They sprout dragon wings and their horns grew longer, and are covered by dense scales.

Other dragonewts usually have ahuman-like appearance such in the case ofSoukaand her subordinates, along with the members ofDragon Faithful. Furthermore, they can also assume a more hybrid form and cover themselves with dragon scales, as well as sprout wings and horns at will.
Background: Dragonewts are descended from dragons that "humanized" themselves and mated with the human race. Over time, the dragonfactorof certain populations got diluted, resulting in a lesser form known as lizardmen. It is possible for lizardmen to evolve into dragonewts by beingnamedby a powerful individual.
Trivia: In the story, human-type dragonewts are sometimes said to have tails in addition to wings and horns, but this trait is absent from all of their "official" descriptions, LN illustrations, and manga and anime depictions.

Dino.title: Dino

Appearance: Dino has the appearance of a youthful man that could be described as beautiful if it weren't for the rings under his eyes and his sleepy mannerisms. He has messy purple-silver hair and dull grey-blue eyes, as well as six pairs of wings, six black feathered and six white feathered, that he normally keeps hidden.
Dino's usual attire consists of a purple-pink shirt, white pauldrons, and a green cloak. He can usually be seen wearing his twin swords sheathed around his waist.
Personality: Dino, as the title "Sleeping Ruler" implies, is a lethargic individual who finds solace in wasting his time on extended periods of sleep. Despite his indolent nature, he maintains a keen concern for his public image and prefers not to be the sole standout figure. Unabashed despite his status as aDemon Lord, he exhibited a swift expectation forRimuruto provide him with accommodations and sustenance, displaying a degree of shamelessness.

Dino possesses a proclivity for deflecting blame and evading responsibility. WhenGuy Crimsonquestioned him about thePrimordialsand his failure to intervene in Rimuru's naming process, Dino promptly shifted the blame onto Rimuru, demonstrating his inclination to sidestep trouble. Additionally, he is easily swayed by gestures of goodwill, as seen when Rimuru offered him cream puffs; enamored by the food, Dino humorously pledged to become Rimuru's subordinate.

His sojourn atTempesthas brought about notable changes in Dino's disposition. Initially hesitant to engage in work, the allure of high-quality food, engaging entertainment, and an interesting job transformed him into a dedicated researcher. Dino's commitment to his friends is evident; even under Michael'sUltimate Dominion, he hesitated to confront them and only escalated his efforts when faced with adversity. This unwavering dedication led him to betray Feldway, a former colleague and superior, in order to assist in defeatingVega.
Background: Dino, like the rest of the Seven Angels of Origin, was born at the genesis of creation as a servant and chief advisor to the "Star King Dragon"Veldanava. By Veldanava's side, Dino served as his sword on the battlefield, becoming the greatest swordsman of that time. When the world was pacified and strife vanished, Veldanava tasked Dino with the role of the watcher, overseeinghumanityand reporting their actions.

In accordance with this task, Dino traveled the world withPicoandGarasha, two other members of the Seven Angels of Origin. However, during Dino's absence, tragedy struck. Veldanava and his wifeLuciawere both murdered by terrorists from another nation. Consumed by murderous rage, Dino unleashed hisUltimate skill,Astarte, destroying the nation responsible. Yet, this revenge did not bring solace. Upon regaining reason, Dino found that everything had lost its meaning.

Contemplating destroying theworlditself, he realized the futility of such an action. Dino, rational but lacking positivity, set limits on his actions and sealed off his power of 'Astarte, "Lord of Heaven"' due to feeling responsible for the destruction wrought in passion. This loss of purpose marked the moment when Dino became aFallen Angel.

Fortunately, his colleagues, Pico and Gracia, were with him, preventing his disappearance from the world. Despite thousands of years passing, Dino continued his mission as a watcher, devoid of the meaning of life. His search led him to findMilim, the last remnant and daughter of Veldanava and Lucia. Reluctant to acknowledge Milim as his master, Dino observed her from the shadows, allowing Pico and Gracia to gather information while he lived in idleness, eventually becoming a Demon Lord.

When Milim went out of control, Guy andRamirisintervened, and Dino assisted from the shadows, recognizing his role in preventing her from destroying the world. Later, he befriendedDagrueland freeloaded off him, finding a semblance of a daily life as a Demon Lord. However, a significant change occurred duringWalpurgiswhen Rimuru became a Demon Lord.

The shock of witnessingClayman, a perceived weakling, strike Milim awakened something within Dino. Concerned about Milim losing control, Dino investigated and discovered that Rimuru was the cause. Intrigued, he found a new meaning of life by touching the essence of Rimuru, a moment that felt like destiny rather than coincidence. This encounter ignited a newfound interest in Rimuru and marked a turning point in Dino's existence.

Appearance: Tear is a small and youthful girl with magenta hair tied into short twin-tails. She wears a harlequin outfit and dons a mask with a teardrop motif and two red horns.
Personality: Tear is a childish and playful but also somber and sweet girl. Though the burden of her power placed an immense strain on her spirit that prevented her from maturing, she was by no means an unintelligent person during that period. She was more than capable of fooling others and constructing well-thought out plans to achieve her goals when needed. She absolutely hates being treated like a kid, often admonishingLaplaceandClaymanfor doing so.

During the events ofRumbling of Heaven and Earth, Tear's spirit finally caught up to her power and she was able to fully mature. This was caused by the recognition that she was the only one left to protectKagali, only further enhanced by the transplanted fragments of Clayman's core that healed her injuries from the volume prior.
Background: Originally anElfduring the era of the Great Sorcerous Nation Of Soma, Tear was the personal maid of theHigh elfPrincess Kagali. When Kagali's father was taken over by the Evil SorcererJahiland outwardly seemed to have gone insane, she was one of the people inside the castle that remained loyal to Kagali after she was turned into theDeathmanKazalim. When a youngMilim Nava–enraged at the actions taken against her by Jahil–obliterated the castle in Soma, Tear was one of the individuals resurrected by Kagali alongsideFootmanand Clayman.

When Kagali saw that the appearances of the three of them weren't scarred by becoming Deathmen while she was cursed to look like a rotting corpse, she became depressed, with the three of them deciding to wear masks to match with hers from that day forward. The four of them were later joined by the newly born Laplace and they regrouped with the elven survivors still loyal to Kagali to create the nation ofJistav, eventually also forming theModerate Harlequin Alliance.

He was revived at the entrance empty-handed. This left him fuming.[3]

During thecouncilmeeting attended by Tempest representatives inEnglassia, he was used as a pawn by the Rosso family in one of their plots and attempted to challenge Rimuru, only to face an overwhelming defeat at the hands ofShuna, following which he was apprehended by local authorities. Viola.title: Viola

Appearance: Viola represents an iron humanoid figure with a body cloaked beneath a long dark robe or mantle complete with a hood covering its head.

Viola's metallicbodypossesses a prominent light grey color of metallic. Its constituent parts are in great condition giving rise to a body without the appearance of being rusted or any other signs of metal corrosion. Due to its smooth surface and the bright color of the metal, with the right level of illumination, reflections can be seen.
To acquire a more manicured appearance which doesn't overtly expose the Golem's true structure, Viola sports a lengthy, dark colored hooded, short-sleeved cloak. It extends to the level of the knees.

Similar to its creator in combat form, Viola possesses a double pair of arms, allowing it to wield, control and even juggle various projectiles of energy and magic, as well as hold other weapons such as spears and swords, with great ease and efficiency. Each of its forearms is wrapped in some manner of bandages or tourniquets.

The head of Viola has an oval shape, with a protruding chin or mouth, and distinctive hexagonal eye sockets containing golden vision devices that serve as eyes. Also Viola's head has hollows on the each side imitating the ears, which are difficult to notice due to the permanently worn hood.
Personality: Viola exhibits no personality characteristics whatsoever. Although Clayman is genuinely and openly proud of his powerful engineering, Viola is not a subordinate of Clayman in the conventional sense, but rather a majestic weapon that tears enemies apart protecting its builder.
Background: In the days when the Curse Lord, the formidable and intimidating LordKazalim, reigned overJistav, he devised numerous protective measures and protocols to preserve the ruined city ofAmrita, which lies beneath the futureClayman's castle. Kazalim, being an accomplished creator of weaponised Golems, had himself created an army of golems to safeguard the underground ruins. Clayman, who was preparing for his upcoming role as Demon Lord, inherited the technique of creating magic dolls from his mentor and master, eventually bringing his best work, Viola, to life.[1]
Trivia: In themangaadaptation compared to theanimeadaptation, Viola's body was more heavily covered in a robe and concealed by darkness.
It has been stated that Viola's body possesses aUnique-gradequality.[2]From this, it can be surmised and interpreted that the metal that was used to sculpt its body is most probablymagisteel.
Viola's ability to hurl swords and spears, which similarly to its body possessed a Unique Quality, was not visualized in the anime adaptation.

AfterRamirisand Beretta had moved toTempestand established theDungeon, Beretta finally had the opportunity to give the spoils of war to itssummoner, originally intended as a reward in exchange for their relocation. Albeit Viola was teeming with a gigantic variety of Unique-grade weaponry, they turned out to be difficult-to-modify, rendering them useless for Ramiris' scientific studies.[3]Most likely they had become prized and coveted bounties in the treasure chests of the Dungeon, or had been sold for a substantial fortune by Rimuru.

Clayman was delighted to demonstrate his man-made masterpiece onWalpurgis, and was immensely proud of his creation. However, although Viola was actually superior to Clayman in terms of direct combat prowess, in comparison to the Golems defending the ruins of Amrita, it stood only marginally better than the average.[4]

Creation: While natural born golems born frommagiculesdo exist, most golems are the constructs of mages. The most common materials for crafting golems are clay, iron, stone, and wood. A golem can be a hand-made creation such as a doll or stuffed toy, or it can be animated from its raw components with thecreation magicspell 'Create Golem'.
Usage: Once a golem has been crafted there are two options available to the user. They have the option of controlling the golem directly with their own energy throughartsor they can have the golem be inhabited by a living spirit, most commonly that of anelementalordaemon. Users of the former method are referred to asgolem mastersand make for extremely formidable opponents in combat. In cases of the latter type of golem, control circuits are usually magically implanted within the golem's body which gives the master of the golem complete control over its physical actions, similar to the locking curse placed onotherworlders. This degree of control over the golem's actions while they still act autonomously makes them extremely popular amongDemon Lordsfor physical labor such as farming and mining.

Personality: Blanche was a kind, sweet, shy, innocent, and vastly intelligent girl who loved books and was renowned as a genius. She was satisfied to simply rule over her kingdom and lead it to prosperity alongside her friend Blanc and lover Guinias. She harbored a deep darkness inside of her heart, one born from the death of her mother and the neglect of her father. It was only amplified even further by the betrayal of Guinias, which resulted in her suicide.
Background: Around 3000 years ago the first monarch and queen of the Silberia Kingdom achieved the unthinkable and made a deal with the White Primordial Blanc. The deal entailed Blanc acting as the kingdom's Guardian Deity and in return, the royal family would give birth to her vessel someday. With the pact sealed by magic, the heirs of the Silberia royal family were all born with immense magical power and crimson eyes that could see through everything.

3000 years later, a perfect vessel was finally born to the royal family. This vessel was Blanche, a girl with unimaginable magic power, white hair, and trademark crimson eyes that served as proof of the pact. She lived happily alongside her mother and maids in their private villa.

When Blanche turned 12, her mother passed away. The maids and servants who were kind to her had long since been removed by the cruel efforts of the second queen, who rose to power within the palace 2 years prior. Her father the king only had eyes for her half-sister Ashera, and so Blanche was left truly alone.

Coincidentally, however, 12 was the age at which Blanche was considered an adult by ancient custom. And in accordance with their pact, Blanc made herself known to Blanche and offered her a single wish in exchange for her body. Blanche, completely bewitched by the otherwordly beauty of Blanc, completely ignored the promise she had made to her mother when she was 9 and cared only about Blanc, who was the only one in the world who needed her. Blanche spoke the wish that began to rise from the bottom of her heart and stated it to the enchanting woman before her: "Will you be my friend?". Blanc, who should've been offended by this request, strangely found the concept appealing and by some whim or another, ended up agreeing.

With Blanc by her side, the once timid Blanche became filled with confidence and slowly but surely started making a foothold for herself in the palace. Whether it was history, maths, geology, arts, etiquette, or even magic, Blanche was considered a genius among geniuses. She even became engaged to Guinias Nam Grunce, the second son of an influential family in the Namrium Kingdom. She fell completely in love with him and the two soon became the exact image of an ideal couple.

However, things were not as rosy as they seemed. When it came to light that Guinias had only been using her to get to Blanc and that their nation was endangered by her naive love, Blanche fell back into an immense depression. Despite the begging and pleading of Blanc, who declared her love for Blanche more important than anything else, Blanche executed the contract between the two of them and handed herbodyover to Blanc in an act of suicide.

Mokshan.summary:
NON-CANON CONTENTThis article covers non-canon creations that might not have been produced by the author of the light novel series.

Summary: NON-CANON CONTENTThis article covers non-canon creations that might not have been produced by the author of the light novel series.
A second and third one would be born from the first one's desires to be still be the strongest of the Loup Loupe, with the third one successfully escaping into the Central World.
Appearance: Mokshan looks nearly identical to Clayman, with the exception of his purple hair, yellow eyes and black suit compared to Clayman’s white suit.
The Third Mokshan looks the same as pseudo-awakened Clayman.
Personality: Mokshan is ambitious, wanting to escape the Loup Loupe, absorb allmagiculesfrom theCentral Worldand turn theMirror Worldinto the one true world.

He was also known to be a cunning and a clever strategist, as seen how he was able to useMarionette Heartto escape the Loup Loupe by forcing themajinon the lower floors to wish for his escape, a feat which no one else could do, and even used it to force the residents of theMad Cityto sacrifice themselves whenever they are about to die in order to create stronger copies of themselves. To maintain the space, he used the corpses of the copies as feed. In addition to that, knowingVeldoraandDiablo’s powers, withEmils’ aid he transformed the Mad City residents intoOrcinus Altersto prevent them from intervening.

Mokshan was also noted to mock Izis a lot, as seen how he “sympathized” with her and mocked her for not being able to understand her own ‘‘daughter’s’’ emotions. He even laughed when Veldora said Izis was a “crazy witch” who lived inside a mirror, noting how they were mocking her. When Izis called off their plan, he mocked her, saying her words sounded like the words of a sheltered princess, and afterHyuga’s defeat asked whether being young wasn’t advantageous. He mocks her further and states that the more pawns she creates the more pawns he also gets.
He is also very proud of himself for being the only Majin who was able to escape the Loup Loupe, calling himself as the "president" of the tower.

In addition to that, Mokshan also despises being known as a forgery, sharing Emils' beliefs and even claiming that the forgeries were also living creatures with beating hearts. He feels insulted by this, and wishes to prove that he and the other forgeries were not only equal to their original counterparts, but even better than them.

At the same time however, he also detests and fears only one thing alone, and that is being controlled by others. He is willing to use any means necessary to prevent himself from being controlled, and is ready to even kill anyone who tries to snatch his freedom away.
The third Mokshan shares the memories and the personality of the original one as well as the second one.
Background: Mokshan was created from the Loup Loupe made by Izis, the Mirror Witch as an unexpected result of an experiment she seemingly abandoned. Created on the basis of the Demon Lord Clayman, by gaining a similar body and through a chain of nameless Majin, Mokshan found himself entrapped within the Loup Loupe tower. Desiring to escape, the fakeDeathman, having access to Clayman's abilities utilized his Marionette Heart curse to control all the nameless monsters and force them to wish for his escape, thus resulting in him getting out of the tower and arriving in the Mirror World.

Having found out that the tower existed within the Mirror World, a disappointed Mokshan eventually notices the Witch of the Mirror, Izis, who was plotting to take downRimuruin order to escape from the Mirror World and approaches her, who only learns later about Mokshan's creation. Mocking the Mirror Witch for not being able to understand about her own daughter, the fake Deathman mocks her and suggests her to useMegalomaniaon her by combining with the infinity mirror. He convinces her to do so after stating he was the only one to actually escape from the Loup Loupe. Izis agrees to grant Mokshan control over the infinity mirror but asks him to take care of her. He agrees, claiming that she is the key to escaping from the Mirror World and begins the infinity mirror process.

Within the infinity mirror, Mokshan asks Izis to amplifyShinsha's desires, resulting in the creation of an incomplete copy ofTempest's city and a Mirrored copy of Rimuru Tempest, who takes on the name of Emils and the three of them ally together to transform the Mirror World into the Mad City, a city and a world much better than Tempest.

However, Mokshan had a secret motive of himself for allying with Izis. The fake Deathman, being ambitious as ever, was planning to transform the empty Mirror World itself into the Central World. Knowing the principles of the Loup Loupe, the working of the infinity mirror as well as Izis'skillarsenal, Mokshan used both of these powers together to not only create a new environment but combine both the worlds together into a single world.

After his defeat by Izis he is sent back to Loup Loupe, which he noticed and refused to be surpassed, his desire to be stronger resulted in a second and then third Mokshan being born with the latter successfully escaping to the Central World. He desired revenge on Rimuru where he temporarily traps their subordinates, but eventually Shinsha defeats him. Back in the Mirror World he attempted to forcefully make Emils obey him, but Emils defeats him instead.
Trivia: The word "Mokshan" (解脱者) stands for 'Liberated'. Mokshan is a word derived from the Sanskrit word "Moksha", which means the release from the samsara (world) and liberation from one's karma (the result of the actions of a person's past and present lives) in order to attain nirvana (the final goal in Buddhism that surpasses karma, samsara and suffering). Mokshan befits his name, as he was trapped within the Loup Loupe tower and freed himself.

Individuals born from Loup Loupe tower seem to possess a different personality than that of their base templates unlike the copies of individuals made by Megalomania, in the sense that they do not possess their base template's memories and experiences. The same goes for both Mokshan and Shinsha, who despite being made and appearing similar to their base templates, have absolutely no idea about their base templates let alone share their personality traits, with Shinsha herself knowing about Rimuru through Izis, while Mokshan only knows that he gained Clayman's body.

While Marionette Heart was only a special curse that was used by the Demon Lord Clayman to make individuals into his puppets, Mokshan was able to use the curse to increase his own power itself. It should be noted that while the curse operates the same way in both the Central World and the Mirror World, both have different mechanics due to the laws of the respective worlds they are used in.

He is the only character in the event where he is not fought as an actual Boss or any enemy unit either despite him playing a major role in the story event and being the mastermind behind the Mad City's creation.

Izis noted that Mokshan was easy to defeat due to the fact that he was created through a chain of nameless majin, implying that if he was created through named majin instead, he would be a formidable foe.Though the third Mokshan born from the desires of the first and second one's desires, he was a formidable foe.

During the events of the story, he becomes close with the members of the Coleus royal family, with him deciding to stay and declare his allegiance to them after the plots ofKarlandGustavare dealt with. For his valor and strength, he was officially knighted, and he quickly rose to the position of captain.

Background: When he was still an apprentice, The small nation he studied abroad at was trampled by Demon Lord Valentine's army. Someone rushed to that nation—Hinata Sakaguchi who just became a Holy Knight at the time. When surrounded by a horde of monsters, it only took a swing of her thin sword to wipe them all out. Since then, Leonard was fascinated with the charm of swordsmanship.

While researchingElemental magicon one hand, he could not forget the sights of Hinata's sword, thus he practiced repeatedly using a wooden sword while imitating her. He soon mastered theartand returned to his academy inKingdom of Englassia. There he studiedAspectual magicand waited patiently for the chance of moving to theHoly Empire of Lubelius.

It was not easy for foreigners to immigrate to Holy Empire of Lubelius, but if it was a believer of Luminas with outstanding achievement, he may be granted permission. However, it would come at the price of severing ties with his family. Leonard chose to migrate without any hesitation. His mastery of both Aspectual and Elemental Magic got him the permission to immigrate.

Later he studiedHoly magicin Lubelius and was able to earn a place as an apprentice knight in the Templar Order. During theelementalcontract ceremony, he formed contract with an Elemental of light and became a "Saint Wizard": a Master of Aspectual, Elemental, and Holy magic.

He was the Holy Knight of light, just as reflected from his pure and noble soul. It didn’t take Renard too long after becoming aHoly Knightto become an adjutant of the person he looks up to—Hinata. This is the result of his active initiatives in partaking challenging tasks and achieving impressive feats from them.

Gabiru and his men were assigned to cultivateHipokute grassin theSealed Cave. When they started living there, they doubled as the cave's guards.
Gabiru began to walk around the cave as if he owned the place, sometimes even being referred to as its king. Themonstersinhabiting it also flee at the sight of him.
Ahead of theNasca Namrium Ulmeria United Eastern Empire's invasion of theGreat Jura Forest, they joined theBlue Numbers— and later theWyvern Riders— in theThird Corpsunder the command of Gabiru.

At the beginning, they could take down aEvil centipedewith just the five of them. Some of Gabiru's subordinates have been able to defeat the centipede alone, and now consider the cave as their territory. They have the ability to use breath-type abilities of variousattributesdepending on the individual.[1]They have also acquired flying abilities that allowed them to shoot their breath from the sky.

Each are at least A-ranked. After theHarvest Festival, they acquiredDragon BodyandFlame BreathorThunder Breathabilities. Though their efficiency dropped, their power greatly increased. Though they haven't obtained any newresistances, they did have high resistance, to begin with. With their scale armor being strong as steel, only a direct strike can penetrate their armor. So being able to fly puts them at an overwhelming advantage over their enemies.

Appearance: A youthful woman with medium length brown hair and purple eyes. The green portion of her hair is done up in twintails that rest neatly on her shoulder and are held in place by golden jewelry. She wears a simple but elegant white tube-style dress accented with an orange skirt that's attached by her belt. She has golden rings around the tops of her arms and neck as well as a large golden ornament on her belt.
Personality: Towa is a kind and forthright queen who works ceaselessly for the benefit of her people and is all too willing to sacrifice her life for those important to her. While honest to a fault, she can also be slightly calculating, a fact she admitted to when she divulged toRimuruher reasons for savingHiiro's life. She stated that beyond just wanting to help him, some part of her also wished that he would feel indebted to her and remain by her side. Due to her strong sense of responsibility, she was racked with guilt and shame by this side of her, criticizing herself as unfair and selfish. After receiving some soothing words of encouragement from Rimuru, she eventually learned to accept that part of her.
Like all her predecessors, Towa has a certain integrity present in her character, earning her the admiration and respect ofUltima.
Story: Towa is the reigning queen of the smallKingdom of Raja. She has used the magical power of her tiara, which has been passed down in the royal family from generation to generation to neutralize the poison in the mines of her country and protect the people of Raja. However, the price to pay for this was acursethat ate away at her life. Little did she know, this whole ordeal is a game played by Violet to turn her into a new vessel. Rimuru was soon able to help cure her condition, but she regained it thanks toLacua, who is working forViolet. Following Lacua's defeat, she sacrificed herself to save Hiiro, but Violet revives her as a reward for all the entertainment she and her foremothers gave her and also as an apology for her negligence in overseeing the situation, which allowed Lacua's actions (his meddling violated the terms of the original deal between Violet and the royal family, forcing Violet to terminate the contract and her game).
Sometime later, she took part in Tempest's festival and is among the audience watching the marital arts tournament. She would later have drinks with Rimuru and others.
Relationships: Hiiro: After saving his life, he swore loyalty to her. In fact, the two appear to have a very caring relationship.
MobujiandRaja Minister: They had served her for a long time.
Lacua andChikuan: They intended to make her into a new vessel for Violet, but thanks to Lucua deciding to take matters into his own hands, the plan was foiled.
Violet: She planned to make Towa into a vessel for her, but her scheme was thwarted when Lucua unintentionally meddled with her game.
Rimuru Tempest: She formed good terms with the monster king.

Background: On the ruins of Soma, which was once the Great Sorcerous Nation Of Soma of the Elves in the past, theChaos Dragonappeared and terrorized its surroundings.Sarion Grimwald, the father ofElmesia, who would later found a nation in his namesake, was sent to dispatch it but was defeated in battle. A masked figure in robes approached the dyingChosen herowho had sustained serious injuries from the Chaos Dragon. Kagali, who went by the name Kazalim at the time, offered to resurrect Sarion, with a risk of losing his memories in the process and becoming her puppet. Sarion acquiesced to this. Using the forbidden spellBirthday, Kagali unified the tens of thousands of corpses in the surroundings to create a vessel to board the will of Sarion. Sarion became aDeathman, losing his memories in the process. That encounter birthed the "Curse Lord" Kazalim and the "Wonder Pierrot"Laplace.

Tear,Footman, andClaymanwere already born by then. Kagali named each of them, and considered them her sweet, lovely children. Clayman was created with the intended purpose to see if majin capable of awakening intotrue demon lordscould be artificially produced. He was Kagali's most trusted subordinate and she even inducted him into theDemon Lord council. He was specifically engineered to be a cunning mastermind and a tactical commander, similar to herself.

Tear and Footman were created to have formidable combat prowess that could make them a potential match against aDemon Lord. Even though their intelligence suffered, they compensated with sheer strength. Tear cannot recall her past in significant detail but describes it as a "mixture of memories and feelings". She was once the maidservant to Kagali. While Footman's backstory is unknown, he, like Tear, can't recall his past either.

After learning of this from Laplace, Yuuki and Clayman knew that they had to do something about Rimuru.[1]
Attack of the Demon LordArc: Tear managed to gain the info that Demon LordFreyfeared the return ofCharybdis, and shared this info with Clayman. Clayman then offered Frey to eliminate the threat in exchange for a favor.

Footman and Tear incitedPhobioto become the host of Charybdis in order to exact revenge against Demon LordMilim Nava.[2]As a result, Charybdis was eliminated by the combined effort ofRimuruand Milim, and Clayman earned the bargaining chip he desired.
Human-Monster InteractionArc: Clayman and Yuuki later formed a plan to defeat Rimuru and destroy his nation usingFalmuthandHinata Sakaguchi, but this failed when Rimuru faked his death to trick Hinata, freed Clayman's slaveMjurranfrom his control and tricked him into believing that she died, and destroyed Falmuth's army, usingVeldoraas a front. Clayman, Laplace, Yuuki, and the rest of the group completely fell for this, to which Clayman got the idea of turning Veldora into a puppet. Laplace warned him about his arrogance getting the better of him.
The Octagram SoarsArc: Laplace spoke with Yuuki and Kagali to arrange another plan to defeat Rimuru using Frey and Milim, who is brainwashed by Clayman using anOrb of Dominationthat Yuuki and Kagali gave him. While Clayman went to theWalpurgis, Laplace tried to infiltrate theWestern Holy Churchto try and find out the secret behind it. Footman and Tear helped to observe the war between Clayman's army and Milim'sDragon Faithfulagainst the combined forces ofJura-Tempest FederationandBeast Kingdom of Eurazania. Phobio andGeldambushed them, as the former wanted revenge on them for tricking him. Tear and Footman were too powerful for them, but left them alone after that as they were not ordered to kill them. However, this was Geld and Phobio's true intentions so to ensure that Rimuru's army would win and that they would be ready for them in the future. Yuuki and Clayman's plan to eliminate Rimuru fell apart due to Rimuru (who had become ademon lord) and Veldora being involved in the meeting, Frey revealing that she was never on Clayman's side, and Milim revealing that she was faking her brainwashing and that Kagali's neckless didn't work on her at all (which Yuuki and the entire Alliance failed to realize), resulting in Clayman's demise. Meanwhile, Laplace is caught by Hinata and had to flee the church, knowing that he can't beat her. Once learned about Clayman's death fromRoy Valentin, he killed thevampireout of anger.[3]
Conflict Between Saints and MonstersArc: They were seen mourning the death of Clayman and had to lay low for the time being, but Yuuki still intends to continue his plans. Laplace blamed Clayman's reckless actions for the reason why their plan to defeat Rimuru was a failure while Yuuki also sees that he had underestimated how the Demon Lords would respond to the situation.
The Majin Behind the ScenesArc: Kagali and Yuuki went into the ruins together with Rimuru, Milim,Gobta,Ranga, andShion, as a trap set up byMariabell Rosso.
Awakening of the Chosen HeroArc: Together with Yuuki, they conspired withGranbell Rossoin order to stealLuminous' ultimate weapon. They succeeded in unleashing the "weapon", but realized that they've been tricked by Granbell.
Abilities: The weakest member of the Moderate Harlequin Alliance is at least at ademon lord seed's level. In terms of strength, Laplace is leading while Tear and Footman are not far behind.

Clayman on the other hand was not that powerful compared to his fellow members being the weakest especially in terms of raw physical power, but definitely made up for it as the most educated and dexterous of the group through plotting and creating various schemes and tactics.
Trivia: Kagali wore a mask and a robe to hide her disfigured face. It was shameful for her to look heavily scarred. That's why all members of Moderate Harlequin Alliance hide their true faces with masks, in order to share in Kagali's suffering and because they stand in solidarity with their master.
This group had a much smaller role in the web novel compared to the light novel. In the web novel, its members except Clayman only appeared during the Great Tenma War arc, the final arc of the story.

Clayman hid his relationship with the Moderate Harlequin Alliance upon becoming a Demon Lord as he feared it could lead to an undesirable outcome in the future. The same applies with Kagali, who, during her tenure as Demon Lord Kazalim hid her relationship with her creations. However, it is eventually revealed that he's a part of the Jesters during Volume 6 where he refuses to sell out his friends and master to Rimuru.

Ironically, it's the clowns' schemes that aidedJura-Tempest Federationinto becoming a superpower that poses the greatest threat to them, beginning with theOrc Lord's rampage. It's their schemes that forced Rimuru and co. to seek allies and powerup themselves.

infobox.title: Vesta
infobox.Web Novel: Chapter 17: The Outcome of the Promise

Appearance: Unusual for a dwarf, Vesta possesses a slender build and stands rather tall, around the height of an average human. During his tenure as a minister in Dwargon, he would adorn a white cloak fastened by two intricate golden brooches. This cloak would drape over a long, crisp white shirt, concealed further by a rich, dark brown coat. His attire was often accompanied by an arrogant smirk, exuding an air of confidence.

In his current phase, he has adopted a markedly different style. Vesta now dons a white coat that befits the appearance of a dedicated researcher, signifying his transformation. His attire is complemented by a pair of glasses that enhance his scholarly demeanor, suggesting a profound change in his character.
Personality: Initially introduced as an unlikable bureaucrat, Vesta has undergone a profound transformation since his relocation to Tempest. He embarked on a journey of self-reflection, leading to genuine remorse for his past actions. Demonstrating remarkable growth, he consistently seizes opportunities to extend heartfelt apologies toKaijin, even when the latter has already forgiven him. Vesta's commitment to making amends is evident through his relentless dedication to research and development, pushing his mental and physical limits. His drive stems from a deep desire to not only repayRimuru's kindness but also to mend the trust he once shattered withGazel, whom he had previously disgraced.

Vesta's unexpected utility lies in his affinity for science rather than politics, standing as a testament to his true calling. He has found his purpose in the realm of scientific exploration, displaying talents that greatly benefit the nation of Tempest.
Background: Vesta, born as the son of a marquis, was deeply inspired by Gazel's presence from his early years. His determination to be of utmost use to Gazel led him to join the Dwarven Engineering Corps, where he assumed the role of Kajin's second-in-command. Despite their common goals, Vesta frequently clashed with Kaijin due to the latter's commoner background, exacerbated by Kaijin's close association with Gazel.

The corps initiated a pioneering endeavor, the magic-armor soldier project, which Vesta ardently pursued. Despite Kaijin's caution about the project's hastened pace, Vesta disregarded the advice. A failed experiment brought the project to a standstill, prompting Vesta to unjustly lay the blame on Kaijin. In an act of true integrity, Kaijin took full accountability and resigned from the corps. Yet, even after Kaijin's departure, Vesta's antagonism persisted, disrupting Kaijin's work as a skilled blacksmith.

Vesta's campaign of harassment finally met its end when Kaijin physically confronted him after Vesta's disrespectful attitude towards Rimuru Tempest. Vesta's retaliation led to a legal battle in Dwargon's court, culminating in Kaijin and his companions' banishment. However, Gazel, who observed the proceedings, chose to remain silent. Following the trial, Gazel privately confronted Vesta, exposing his deceit concerning the magic-armor soldier project. Overwhelmed by Gazel's disappointment, Vesta crumbled under the weight of his guilt, with Gazel instructing him to never appear before him again.

A chance for redemption emerged when Gazel orchestrated Vesta's kidnapping, transporting him to Tempest to undergo a transformation. Here, Vesta had the opportunity to mend his ways and rebuild trust with Gazel by contributing to the betterment of Tempest. Ultimately, Vesta ascended to the position of head researcher, culminating in the successful completion of the full potion project. In this capacity, he became instrumental in educating Tempest's staff about etiquette, fostering growth and cohesion within the nation.
Trivia: In the anime, Vesta bears an eerie similarity to Amshel Goldsmith fromBlood+during his time in Dwargon.
Ground-dwelling dragon steak was one of the meals served at the end ofWalpurgisduringConflict Between Saints and Monsters.

Appearance: Cazac appeared to be a well-dressed man who wore clothes of fine quality. However, to those with a discerning eye it was evident the clothes he wore were out of fashion. Falling on hard times as a noble, Cazac could not afford to wear clothes in fashion that would otherwise be expected from a man of his title.
Personality: Cazac was, among many things, a swindler who engaged in theft and fraud. He employed various dishonest practices in his daily business, on the light side peddling random junk as pricey antiques to turn a quick profit. He held no regard for international laws, even dipping his fingers in the trafficking ofdemi-humanswhich eventually spelled his doom. He hates it when his deals are called off and will resort to taking revenge on those who decline his offers.
Story: He came to see Gard to try and obtain elf slaves, though Gard quietly realizes that he is a criminal and attempts to think of a way to turn him down. When Rimuru came in, Cazac was annoyed with their interruption. Taking an interest in Rimuru, he decides to take them as his new slave. Gard, angered by this, kicks him out and ends his business with him. Cazac left in a rage, vowing revenge. To this end, he sent a monster to attack Gard, but one of Rimuru's subordinates foils this plot. Upon learning of Cazac's demi-human trafficking operations, Rimuru decides to take him down and rescue his slaves, and sends Souei to deal with this. However, it is later discovered that his operation was stopped by Masayuki and he was arrested.
Relationships: Gard Mjöllmile: He once came to see him to obtain elf slaves, but once he decided to take Rimuru as a slave, Gard did not take that kindly and cuts ties with him, leading an outraged Cazac to swear revenge. He sent a monster to attack Gard, but this ploy was foiled by one of Rimuru's subordinates.

Rimuru Tempest: He tried taking them as a slave, but Gard did not allow this. Once Rimuru learns of his misdeeds, they sought to take down his operations, but Team Lightspeed beat them to it. On the other hand, Cazac had no idea of their true characteristics as a slime and Demon Lord.

infobox.title: Gard Mjöllmile
infobox.Japanese: ガルド・ミョルマイル
infobox.Alternate Translation(s): Garde MyourmileGarde MyourmilesGard MjollmileGard Mjolmire[1]Garudo Mjolmile
infobox.Title(s): Grand MerchantDon of the UnderworldSovereign of the Backstreets
infobox.Affiliation(s): Ministry of Treasury/FinancesThree Wise DrunksFour Nations Trade Alliance

Appearance: He is a man of modest stature, characterized by a plump physique that lends him an amiable presence. His distinctive features include a well-groomed handlebar mustache coupled with a neatly trimmed goatee. Adding to his unique appearance, a streak of striking yellow hair runs through the center of his locks. This touch of color adds a dash of eccentricity to his overall demeanor, catching the eye of anyone who encounters him.

Since ascending to the position of head of the Four Nations Trade Alliance, Mjollmile's wardrobe has undergone a transformation. He now favors impeccably tailored three-piece suits that radiate an air of opulence and sophistication. The choice of attire further enhances his authoritative aura, complemented by his commanding presence and confident demeanor. Despite his high-ranking role, a perpetually greedy smile graces his lips, hinting at a shrewd business acumen that underpins his success.
Personality: Mjöllmile possesses a remarkable ability to put people at ease through his extensive experience and innate talent as a merchant. His deep understanding of the trade not only allows him to forge connections but also grants him the uncanny ability to gauge a person's character with just a single glance. Despite his occasional crudeness, which he wears unabashedly, he remains unfazed by dealings that might be considered slightly questionable, given his lofty position as the head of a powerful economic conglomerate. However, his perception of boundaries remains intact, and he reserves his loyalty for those he deems worthy of his trust. He is also shown to be very smart, as he was able to recognize Rimuru (who has assumed a different form) after they saved his life and can tell that Cazac is a criminal based on their conversation.

A fearless risk-taker at heart, he carries an unwavering belief in his own luck, often embarking on ventures that others might shy away from. Anchored by the motto "Merchants first and foremost consider both parties' profit," his economic endeavors reflect a balanced perspective that seeks mutual benefit for all involved parties.

Since becoming a member of Rimuru's team, Mjöllmile's initial astonishment at his boss's actions has gradually transformed into a sense of nonchalance. The remarkable occurrences within Rimuru's sphere of influence have become so frequent that Mjöllmile now approaches them with a sense of numb acceptance, having adapted to the extraordinary nature of his environment.
Background: Mjöllmile's journey began as an orphan, a mere seven-year-old selling vegetables just to scrape by and survive. Yet, amidst the challenges, he discovered a profound joy in witnessing the smiles he brought to his customers' faces. This simple but impactful connection with people ignited a passion within him, guiding him onto the path of a merchant. As time passed, his determination and innate business acumen led him to new heights.

Gradually, Mjöllmile managed to establish his own shop in the quaintKingdom of Blumund, and he expanded his influence by establishing a branch in the grandKingdom of Englassia. His relentless dedication paid off as his business began to thrive, and his reputation soared. However, just as he was on the brink of prosperity, a pivotal encounter would change his destiny forever.

The Guildmaster of the Kingdom of Blumund,Fuzeapproached him, introducing him to Rimuru Tempest, a figure of significant influence. Drawn by the prospect of new opportunities and connections, Mjöllmile was invited to join the ranks of Tempest. This offer, while enticing, presented a dilemma. He understood that parting with his established shop in Blumund could potentially be a disadvantage in the future. Therefore, he devised a clever solution – leaving a trusted head clerk in charge of the store, ensuring its continued operation while he ventured into the unknown.

Mjöllmile's decision to accept Rimuru's invitation took him to Tempest, a new realm with untapped potential. His keen eye for potential was not limited to business alone; he recognized the promise within five individuals and their abilities. These individuals, unexpectedly to him, chose to cast aside their current lives in pursuit of a greater future alongside Mjöllmile in the blossoming kingdom of Tempest. The profound loyalty and dedication they displayed caught him off guard, as he had never anticipated that they would willingly abandon their livelihoods to follow him into uncharted territory.

These discreet armaments are a testament to his cautious nature and readiness for any situation. Additionally, his slender build further enhances his agile and nimble demeanor.
Personality: He is notably taciturn, often shrouding his thoughts and emotions in an enigmatic veil. His inscrutable nature adds an air of mystery to his character, making it difficult for those around him to discern his true intentions or sentiments.

Together with his companions, they were able to make it further than any challenger at the time, which caughtRimuru's attention and prompted a look into their backgrounds. They were easily seen through as spies but Rimuru and his staff took no immediate action against them and opted to merely observe them. Upon reaching the 60th floor, they were instantly defeated byAdalmannandAlbert.

After reflecting on their stay inRimuru City, they all expressed their satisfaction with the country and the luxuries that it provided which they miss from their home world. When Gadra cut his ties with the Empire, they followed suit and took up an occupation as researchers for Ramiris.

Appearance: Despite being portrayed as a somewhat stereotypical greedy king, Edmaris is neither short nor fat like one might expect. He is a rather tall and muscular individual, with long blonde hair (grey in the anime) and brown eyes (green in the anime). He used to have a rather large and majestic beard, but shaved it after abdicating from the throne, keeping only a large moustache instead.
Personality: Edmaris was initially a greedy man as described byGazel Dwargo, willing to wage war against theJura-Tempest Federationunprovoked to protect his nation's interests. He was also vindictive, initially refusing aid toEarl Migamduring theOrc Warfor personal reasons. However, he is by no means foolish, and is actually a very competent and also wise  king. He is also fairly popular amongst his people, believing a king's duty is first and foremost to his citizens. Edmaris is pragmatic and tactical, waiting for theWestern Holy Church's approval before instigating his war against Tempest and intending to frame the conflict as if Falmuth was acting in self-defense. On the other hand, he quickly becomes cowardly under pressure, during which he stops thinking rationally, deluding himself that he could strike a deal withRimuru Tempestafter he waged war on his country.

After being tortured byShion, Edmaris' spirit was broken  and he became a willing servant ofDiabloin exchange of mercy for his kingdom,giving up his throne toYoum Farmenasand allowing his country to become a puppet state controlled by Tempest. Still, he has retained much of his former wisdom, being a competent advisor to the new king.
Background: Edmaris was once the king of Falmuth–a nation that would later be reborn as Farmenas–and ruled over it alongside his trusted ministers and advisers. When theWestern Holy Churchdeclared aHoly Waragainst theJura-Tempest Federation, he was eager to spearhead the war as its commander-in-chief. It was a decision he made partly out of greed–as Tempest threatened the stability of his nation's economy–but also in desire to become famed as a Heroic King internationally, a status that would firmly cement his authority to even the highest levels of the nobility.

When his army–over 20,000 strong–marched on Tempest, the king expected a full surrender from its perceived Pacifist leader. Instead it turned into a one-sided massacre that saw the deaths of every last soldier and the birth of a newDemon Lord. After this, Edmaris was brutally tortured as a prisoner of war for weeks on end, eventually submitting to Tempest and agreeing to be the servant of theDaemonDiablo. With Edmaris's aid, the country of Falmuth was easily put into the hands of Tempest and a new puppet king–Youm Farmenas–was installed. Edmaris continues to serve Youm as a Viscount and close advisor, granting vital support to the ravaged country that is but a shell of its former self.

Background: The Composite Division, initially perceived as a disparate group, comprised individuals singled out for their perceived inability to cooperate in groups. This perception stemmed from the public's misunderstanding, as a closer inspection revealed that each member possessed extraordinary abilities. These unique capabilities, rather than a lack of teamwork, were the root cause of the division's coordination challenges.

The group included numerous otherworlders whose potential remained largely unknown. The division housed individuals who, through experiments conducted within its confines, manifested powers beyond comprehension, transforming into formidable magic beasts with strengths surpassing A rank. Despite the difficulties in managing such powerful entities, these individuals proved to be exceptional warriors. Additionally, the division gathered human weapons with powers derived from unidentified sources, consolidating a diverse array of experimental outcomes under its banner.

Initially managed and controlled, the division underwent a significant transformation with Yuuki assuming leadership. This shift elevated the division into an extraordinarily potent asset within the army, boasting a total of approximately 200,000 members. Half of this number consisted of officers and non-combatants, leaving a force of around 100,000 troops as the actual combat force. This group was stationed in Dwargon during the Eastern Empire's initial invasion of Tempest. Upon learning of Yuuki's intention to initiate a coup d'état, the vast majority of its members faced elimination during a purge orchestrated by Velgrynd. Their bodies were repurposed as sacrifices to create new Deathman
Abilities: The members of the Composite Division were characterized by their exceptional and often unpredictable abilities. Many of them were otherworlders with untapped potential, and various experiments conducted within the division led to the emergence of individuals wielding powers beyond conventional understanding. These experimental outcomes resulted in the creation of magic beasts, entities with strengths exceeding the A rank.

Controlling these powerful beings posed challenges, but the division also comprised human weapons whose sources of power remained unidentified. The amalgamation of such diverse abilities and origins created a unique and formidable force. Notably, a hand-picked platoon of approximately 60 elite members, fervently devoted to Yuuki, emerged as the pillars of the Composite Division, further enhancing its combat capabilities.
